newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 96 coffee consumption rose two pct - roasters.
newsitem.headline: French 96 coffee consumption rose two pct - roasters.

text.p: French coffee consumption rose by around two percent in 1996, mostly the result of lower retail prices, the chairman of the French coffee industry and trade association said on Tuesday.
"Provisional data suggest consumption rose by around two percent after falling by an average five percent in 1995 and 1994," Jean-Claude Frankel told Reuters.
He said final consumption data should be available within a month.
"Lower retail prices in 1996 helped consumption slowly return to normal levels," he added.

Asked if French roasters planned to pass on the cost to consumers of a surge in world coffee futures since the start of 1997, Frankel said "To my knowledge higher raw material costs have had no impact on retail prices. To date there has been no increase in retail prices,"
But if futures prices remained at current levels, some roasters were likely to raise retail prices, he said.

Speculative funds buying sparked a new rally in world prices on Monday, with Dutch roaster Douwe Egberts, part of Sara Lee Corp, saying it would raise retail prices by about seven percent on average for a 250-gramme pack.
Coffee futures have risen by about 25 percent since the start of the year, underpinned by concern over tight supplies.
